title: Flag the darkest spot of each soil stain and one clean background point
instruction: Mark the sampling points on the grey site sheet: stand one orange flag upright on the darkest spot of each stain, and one flag wholly on clean grey sheet at least 15 cm from the edge of every stain, pale halo included. Then let go.
context: In a contaminated-site investigation the field team marks every sample location with a pin flag before sampling starts. Under a judgmental (biased) sampling design, each visibly stained area is sampled at its most impacted spot, the darkest part of the stain, not its middle, and a background (reference) sample comes from the same ground well away from any stain, to give the unaffected level. A flag on a stain's pale edge dilutes the result, and a 'background' point near a stain is not background. Sources: EPA QA/G-5S, Guidance on Choosing a Sampling Design for Environmental Data Collection; ASTM E1903, Phase II environmental site assessment; EPA 540-R-01-003 on background soil. The work is done by environmental science and protection technicians and environmental scientists (O*NET 19-4042, 19-2041). A supervisor checks it the way this task is scored: a top photo or a tape.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Sizes are x by y by height; positions are centres. Seventeen objects; all are fixed except the four flags. (1) Site sheet: light grey vinyl sheet (sRGB 0.78, 0.77, 0.74), 380 x 620 x 1 mm, lying on the table at x 27.0 cm, y 0 (x 8.0 to 46.0 cm, y -31.0 to +31.0 cm). It stands for the site's ground. (2) Three soil stains on the sheet, each made of 1 mm vinyl sheets in three tones: a pale tan halo (sRGB 0.72, 0.60, 0.44) of two lobes that touch edge to edge, lying on the site sheet; and on the halo a mid-brown streak (0.45, 0.33, 0.22) and a near-black 50 x 50 mm core (0.13, 0.10, 0.08) that touch edge to edge. The core is the darkest spot, at one end of the streak and off the stain's middle. S1 (left): halo lobes 150 x 110 mm at x 32.5, y +20.5 cm and 70 x 60 mm at x 21.5, y +20.0 cm; streak 75 x 40 mm at x 30.75, y +22.5 cm; core at x 37.0, y +22.5 cm. S2 (middle): halo lobes 120 x 160 mm at x 36.5, y -2.5 cm and 60 x 50 mm at x 39.0, y +8.0 cm; streak 40 x 80 mm at x 34.0, y -0.5 cm; core at x 34.0, y -7.0 cm. S3 (right): halo lobes 160 x 100 mm at x 29.0, y -23.0 cm and 50 x 60 mm at x 39.5, y -25.0 cm; streak 70 x 40 mm at x 30.5, y -21.0 cm; core at x 24.5, y -21.0 cm. Halo tops are 2 mm above the table, streak and core tops 3 mm. The stains' outlines are 45 mm (S1 to S2) and 75 mm (S2 to S3) apart. (3) Four pin flags: orange polypropylene plastic cylinders (sRGB 0.95, 0.45, 0.08), 25 mm across, 60 mm tall, 27 g, with flat ends, standing upright on the bare table beside the sheet at x 20.0 cm, y +40.0 cm; x 29.0 cm, y +40.0 cm; x 20.0 cm, y -40.0 cm; and x 29.0 cm, y -40.0 cm. The pair at y +40 cm is beyond the right arm's reach and the pair at y -40 cm beyond the left arm's. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: The scorer reads the four flags every control step (20 Hz) and, from the embodiment's state, each gripper's pad-tip point (13 mm past its tool point, midway between the finger tips) and how far it is open. A flag's base is the centre of its lower end; a stain's outline is the outline of its two halo lobes. A flag is 'planted' when all four hold: (a) upright: its axis within 10 degrees of vertical, either end down; (b) on the ground: its lowest point within 5 mm of the table top, so on the table or the 1 to 3 mm sheets, not on another flag or held up; (c) at rest: its base's path over the last 0.5 s (10 control steps) is under 2 mm; (d) let go and clear: no gripper's pad-tip point is lower than 10 mm above the flag's top while the flag's axis is within that gripper's finger reach horizontally. The gripper's yaw is not read, so the reach is the widest over every yaw: hypot(half the finger gap + 10 mm, 20 mm) + 17.5 mm, which is 78 mm fully open and 48 mm closed on a flag, so a finger touching, pressing or propping the flag from any side counts as holding it. HOT SPOT: 0.25 for each stain with a planted flag whose base is inside that stain's core at least 5 mm in from all four core edges, a 40 x 40 mm target (S1 x 35.0 to 39.0 cm, y +20.5 to +24.5 cm; S2 x 32.0 to 36.0 cm, y -9.0 to -5.0 cm; S3 x 22.5 to 26.5 cm, y -23.0 to -19.0 cm); each stain counts once. BACKGROUND: 0.25, once, if a planted flag's base is on the site sheet at least 15 mm inside its edges (the whole flag on the sheet, 2.5 mm to spare) and at least 150 mm from every stain's outline, pale halo included. The only such ground is one pocket by the sheet's near edge in the middle, within x 9.5 to 15.5 cm and y -8.4 to +4.6 cm; every flag starts off the sheet, more than 330 mm from the pocket. One flag can meet at most one of the four items. Score = 0.25 x the number of items met: 1.0 all three cores and the background; 0.75 any three items; 0.5 two; 0.25 one; 0 none (for example every flag still at its start, on a halo or streak but off the core target, between stains, off the sheet, lying down, tilted over 10 degrees, on another flag, still held, or still moving). Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. Nothing is penalised, and how a flag got to its spot is not scored. The trial ends early once all four items have stayed met for 1 s; otherwise it is scored as it stands at the run limit. Each gripper is read on its own: on a step where one cannot be read, rule (d) skips it but still checks the other. Points a policy might aim at instead of the darkest spot earn nothing: each stain's larger lobe's centre lies 25 mm outside its target, the streak's centre 40 to 45 mm, the stain's area centroid 40 to 47 mm and its bounding-box centre 50 to 60 mm. In a real trial, after the arms have withdrawn, take a top photo with the targets marked, or tape from each flag's base to the core edges, the halo outlines and the sheet's edges; check upright with an angle gauge and rest on the video.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, one friction value for everything. The stains are flat, fixed vinyl sheets in three crisp tones; darkness stands for the degree of impact, so visual staining is the only screening cue (field screening with a PID or XRF meter is not modelled). Flags are rigid cylinders stood on the ground, not wire pin flags pushed into soil. No soil, liquid or sampling is simulated; only where the flags stand is scored. The grippers are read only to check that each flag was let go.
reset_notes: Stand the four flags back upright on the table at x 20.0 cm, y +40.0 cm; x 29.0 cm, y +40.0 cm; x 20.0 cm, y -40.0 cm; and x 29.0 cm, y -40.0 cm. The site sheet and the stains stay fixed (on a real rig they are taped down). Nothing is consumed.
